title: I asked ChatGPT and Siri AI to build me a workout plan — and there was only one winner
excerpt: ChatGPT and Siri AI made AI-powered workout plans for me, and only one was worth keeping.
content_html:
I’ve been lifting weights at home for a few years now, but recently I’ve found myself stuck in a rut. If anything, my routine has become a humdrum habit, without a clear goal and sense of progression to keep me motivated. Ten exercises, three sets, eight reps, 30 minutes. I’ve run through it so often that I could do it in my sleep.

I’m a true tech lover, so of course I got artificial intelligence (AI) to help me out. Apple has just launched its revamped Siri AI and I’ve been playing around with its early beta edition, so I was curious to know if its new skills extended to solid fitness advice — and if they did, how they held up against the ever-popular ChatGPT.

To find out, I asked each chatbot to dream up a workout routine that could revitalize my fitness habits. After working through both plans and tapping a professional personal trainer for their insights, I was left with the impression that only one of the two workout plans was worth sticking with.

The setup

To start with, I put together a prompt that I then fed into both AIs. The goal was to briefly explain my physical state and outline the kind of workout I was after, noting any constraints such as time and location (I work out at home).

Here’s the prompt I used:

“I am a 36-year-old man in good physical shape who exercises regularly. Create a three-day overall workout plan for me with the goals of hypertrophy and building muscle. The workout will be done in a small home office using dumbbells as the only equipment. It can include calisthenics as well as weighted exercises and should aim to cover different areas of the body. Ensure it lasts no longer than 45 minutes. Explain how often each workout session should be repeated over the course of a week and when rest days should take place, if required.”

I didn’t add any subsequent follow-up messages, as I wanted to know what each AI could come up with given the kind of information that a regular user might provide.

The new challenger: Siri AI

At its Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) in June, Apple made a big song and dance of its new Siri AI virtual assistant, a new foundational model based on Google’s Gemini LLM.

When given my workout prompt, Siri AI put together a plan that included a “push” day focusing on my chest, shoulders and triceps; a “pull” day centered on my back, biceps and rear delts; then a final “legs and core” day. It offered a workout schedule and suggested that each session would take around 45 minutes, with three sets of 8-12 reps and a rest of 60-90 seconds between each set.

“Focus on controlled movements and progressive overload by gradually increasing the weight of your dumbbells or the difficulty of your calisthenics,” it advised. Each exercise was accompanied by a short explanation of how to perform it, which was a welcome touch.

Putting Siri’s action plan into practice, it was obvious that my old self-made workout plan wasn't pushing me hard enough, as the first day’s workout left me feeling like I’d worked harder than I had for months. Off to a good start, I thought.

But Siri’s plan came up well short of 45 minutes, with most days’ efforts lasting a mere 25 minutes. And aside from the lack of warm up, there was also no word on how to complement the exercises with targeted nutritional intake. That’s a serious oversight in its workout regimen, especially for beginners.

To help me better understand the plans from both Siri AI and ChatGPT, I asked personal trainer and fitness coach Scott Laidler for his opinion. Speaking of Siri’s effort, Laidler said that it had a few things going for it.

“Siri’s is simple which means there is little to misinterpret,” said Laidler, adding that “the equipment substitutions are sensible for the office environment.”

While Siri recommends upping the weight as you get stronger, it doesn’t say “what to do once this plan hits diminishing returns, which is months away, not years,” according to Laidler. While it sounds like an open-ended plan, “it’s really only built for a defined window,” Laidler warned, which could “lead to frustration unless you knew to come back to the table and ask for a new plan several times per year.”

That’s a problem inherent in the responses from both Siri and ChatGPT.

The class leader: ChatGPT

While Siri AI’s workout plan was concise, ChatGPT was much longer. It explained what the priorities of the workout were and gave some basic advice, such as aiming to finish with one or two reps in reserve as a guidance on how much weight to use. It then listed a weekly schedule before laying out a simple warm up to perform each session.

Each exercise was listed, with varying numbers of sets and reps, followed by a note on which muscle groups were being targeted. Unlike Siri, there was no explanation of how to perform each exercise, which feels like an oversight with potential for injury. That was a clear win for Siri AI.

At the end, ChatGPT included a “progression” section explaining how to push yourself further, a guide on recovery and nutritional intake, then an explanation of “why this split works.” Taken together, it was a detailed workout plan, if a rather verbose one.

According to Laidler, ChatGPT’s plan was “the better program by some margin.” Siri “applies a flat ‘three sets of 8-12’ to every exercise, with each muscle group trained once a week,” Laidler noted. ChatGPT, on the other hand, “hits most muscle groups twice across the week, varies the sets per exercise, includes a warm up, and gives real progression logic. On paper it’s the more sophisticated plan.”

ChatGPT “is closer to what the literature would see as optimal for the stated goal of gaining muscle,” Laidler stated. “Reps in reserve (RIR) offers a way for the user to keep a reasonable distance from failure, which de-risks the plan especially when training alone.”

OpenAI’s LLM has a trick up its sleeve, too: it can analyze your form based on uploaded videos. I asked it to judge my Romanian deadlift form and it gave me an 8.5 out of ten, giving pointers on what I did well and what could be improved. I wouldn’t take this advice over that of a human expert, but compared to Siri AI — which can’t do any of this at all — it’s another point to ChatGPT.

The overall picture

Despite their individual strengths, Laidler warned that neither Siri AI nor ChatGPT had created an optimal workout plan. As he pointed out, “It doesn’t appear that the LLM has asked follow up questions that may have helped customize the plan a little more.”

This highlights a problem with using AI for personal fitness. While a personal trainer would naturally ask these questions straight away, an AI chatbot won’t necessarily propose them unless prompted. Without a more detailed knowledge of your personal situation, you could end up with a sub-par workout routine that’s not well-suited to your circumstances.

So, if you’re going to use AI to sketch out a fitness plan, make sure to add as much detail in your prompt as possible. Ask it to pose follow-up questions to ensure it has as all the information it needs, and come back to it regularly. Don’t just stick to the plan it gives you and repeat it ad infinitum or you’ll end up like I did: languishing, with your progress grinding to a frustrating halt.

Of course, as Laidler pointed out, the problem with doing this — telling the LLM your injury history, what feels like a hard set, your workout preferences, and more — means that “you need to already know what a well-built program looks like to comprehensively prompt for one.” And if that’s the case, do you even need an AI to help you in the first place?

If you do want to go ahead with an AI fitness coach, ChatGPT is a better bet than Siri AI for now, as it includes more varied sets and targets more muscle groups. Neither is perfect, but Apple has plenty of work to do if it wants to match ChatGPT’s take on fitness advice.

sentences.en: “Siri’s is simple which means there is little to misinterpret,” said Laidler, adding that “the equipment substitutions are sensible for the office environment.”

blocks.html_en: While Siri recommends upping the weight as you get stronger, it doesn’t say “what to do once this plan hits diminishing returns, which is months away, not years,” according to Laidler. While it sounds like an open-ended plan, “it’s really only built for a defined window,” Laidler warned, which could “lead to frustration unless you knew to come back to the table and ask for a new plan several times per year.”

It explained what the priorities of the workout were and gave some basic advice, such as aiming to finish with one or two reps in reserve as a guidance on how much weight to use. It then listed a weekly schedule before laying out a simple warm up to perform each session.

ChatGPT, on the other hand, “hits most muscle groups twice across the week, varies the sets per exercise, includes a warm up, and gives real progression logic. On paper it’s the more sophisticated plan.”

blocks.html_en: This highlights a problem with using AI for personal fitness. While a personal trainer would naturally ask these questions straight away, an AI chatbot won’t necessarily propose them unless prompted. Without a more detailed knowledge of your personal situation, you could end up with a sub-par workout routine that’s not well-suited to your circumstances.

blocks.html_en: So, if you’re going to use AI to sketch out a fitness plan, make sure to add as much detail in your prompt as possible. content_html_zh:
我在家举重已经有几年了，但最近我发现自己陷入了困境。 如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我的日常生活已经变成了一种单调的习惯，没有明确的目标和进步感来保持我的动力。 十次练习，三组，八次，30 分钟。 我经常这样做，以至于我可以在睡梦中完成它。

我是一个真正的科技爱好者，所以当然我有人工智能 (AI) 来帮助我。 苹果刚刚推出了改进后的 Siri AI，我一直在试用它的早期测试版，所以我很好奇它的新技能是否可以扩展到可靠的健身建议，如果可以的话，它们如何与广受欢迎的 ChatGPT 抗衡。

为了找到答案，我要求每个聊天机器人设计一个可以恢复我的健身习惯的锻炼程序。 在研究了这两个计划并听取了专业私人教练的见解后，我的印象是这两个锻炼计划中只有一个值得坚持。

设置

首先，我整理了一个提示，然后将其输入到两个人工智能中。 目标是简要解释我的身体状况并概述我想要进行的锻炼类型，并注明时间和地点等任何限制（我在家锻炼）。

这是我使用的提示：

“我是一名36岁的男性，身体状况良好，经常锻炼身体。 为我制定一个为期三天的整体锻炼计划，目标是增肌和增强肌肉。 锻炼将在一个小型家庭办公室中进行，使用哑铃作为唯一的设备。 它可以包括健美操和负重练习，并且应该旨在覆盖身体的不同部位。 确保持续时间不超过 45 分钟。 解释每次锻炼在一周内应该重复的频率，以及如果需要的话应该在什么时候休息。”

我没有添加任何后续后续消息，因为我想知道每个人工智能根据普通用户可能提供的信息类型可以得出什么结果。

订阅突发新闻、评论、观点、顶级技术交易等。

新的挑战者：Siri AI

在 6 月份的全球开发者大会 (WWDC) 上，苹果公司对其新的 Siri AI 虚拟助手进行了盛大的歌舞，这是一种基于谷歌 Gemini LLM 的新基础模型。

当我收到锻炼提示时，Siri AI 制定了一个计划，其中包括“推力”日，重点锻炼我的胸部、肩膀和三头肌；以背部、二头肌和三角肌后束为中心的“拉力”日；然后是最后的“腿部和核心”日。 它提供了一份锻炼计划，并建议每次训练大约需要 45 分钟，分为三组，每组 8-12 次，每组之间休息 60-90 秒。

它建议：“通过逐渐增加哑铃的重量或体操的难度，专注于受控的动作和渐进的超负荷。” 每个练习都附有关于如何进行的简短解释，这是一个受欢迎的接触。

将 Siri 的行动计划付诸实践，很明显，我以前自制的锻炼计划并没有给我足够的压力，因为第一天的锻炼让我感觉自己比几个月来更加努力了。 我想，这是一个好的开始。

但 Siri 的计划远远低于 45 分钟，大多数日子的努力只持续了 25 分钟。 除了缺乏热身之外，也没有提及如何通过有针对性的营养摄入来补充练习。 这是对其锻炼方案的严重疏忽，尤其是对于初学者而言。

为了帮助我更好地理解 Siri AI 和 ChatGPT 的计划，我向私人教练兼健身教练 Scott Laidler 询问了他的意见。 谈到 Siri 的努力，Laidler 表示它有几个优点。

莱德勒表示：“Siri 很简单，这意味着几乎不会产生误解。”他补充说，“设备替换对于办公环境来说是明智的。”

莱德勒表示，虽然 Siri 建议随着你变得更强壮而增加重量，但它并没有说明“一旦这个计划遇到回报递减的情况该怎么办，这需要几个月的时间，而不是几年的时间”。 虽然这听起来像是一个开放式计划，但“它实际上只是为一个确定的窗口而构建的，”莱德勒警告说，这可能“导致挫败感，除非你知道每年多次回到谈判桌前要求制定新计划。”

这是 Siri 和 ChatGPT 的响应中固有的问题。

班长：ChatGPT

Siri AI 的锻炼计划很简洁，而 ChatGPT 则要长得多。 它解释了锻炼的优先事项，并给出了一些基本建议，例如目标是完成一到两次储备，作为使用多少重量的指导。 然后，它列出了每周的时间表，然后进行了简单的热身以执行每次训练。

每项练习都列出了不同的组数和重复次数，然后附有针对哪些肌肉群的注释。 与 Siri 不同的是，它没有解释如何进行每项练习，这感觉像是一种疏忽，可能会造成伤害。 这对 Siri AI 来说是一场明显的胜利。

最后，ChatGPT 包括一个“进展”部分，解释如何进一步推动自己，恢复和营养摄入指南，然后解释“为什么这种分割有效”。 总而言之，这是一个详细的锻炼计划，尽管是一个相当冗长的计划。

根据 Laidler 的说法，ChatGPT 的计划“在某种程度上是更好的计划”。 Laidler 指出，Siri“对每项练习都采用固定的‘三组 8-12’，每个肌肉群每周训练一次。” 另一方面，ChatGPT“每周对大多数肌肉群进行两次锻炼，每次锻炼的组数不同，包括热身，并提供真正的进展逻辑。 从纸面上看，这是更复杂的计划。”

莱德勒表示，ChatGPT“更接近文献中所认为的增肌目标的最佳状态”。 “预备代表 (RIR) 为用户提供了一种与失败保持合理距离的方法，这可以降低计划的风险，尤其是在单独训练时。”

OpenAI 的法学硕士也有一个妙招：它可以根据上传的视频分析您的表单。 我要求它评价我的罗马尼亚硬拉动作，它给了我 8.5 分（满分 10 分），并指出了我做得好的地方以及可以改进的地方。 我不会接受人类专家的建议，但与 Siri AI 相比（它根本无法做到这一点），这是 ChatGPT 的另一点。

整体图

尽管 Siri AI 和 ChatGPT 各有优势，但 Laidler 警告称，他们都没有制定出最佳的锻炼计划。 正如他指出的那样，“法学硕士似乎没有提出可能有助于进一步定制计划的后续问题。”

这凸显了使用人工智能进行个人健身的一个问题。 虽然私人教练自然会立即提出这些问题，但人工智能聊天机器人不一定会提出这些问题，除非有提示。 如果不更详细地了解您的个人情况，您最终可能会得到不太适合您情况的低于标准的锻炼计划。

因此，如果您打算使用人工智能来制定健身计划，请确保在提示中添加尽可能多的细节。 要求它提出后续问题，以确保它拥有所需的所有信息，并定期回来查看。 不要只是坚持它给你的计划并无限地重复它，否则你最终会像我一样：萎靡不振，你的进步逐渐陷入令人沮丧的停顿。

当然，正如莱德勒指出的那样，这样做的问题是——告诉法学硕士你的伤病史、感觉如何、你的锻炼偏好等等——意味着“你需要已经知道一个完善的计划是什么样子，才能全面提示你制定一个计划。” 如果是这样的话，你首先需要人工智能来帮助你吗？

如果你确实想找一位 AI 健身教练，ChatGPT 目前是比 Siri AI 更好的选择，因为它包含更多样的训练组并针对更多的肌肉群。 两者都不是完美的，但如果苹果想要与 ChatGPT 的健身建议相匹配，它还有很多工作要做。
